newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania to ban pyramid schemes, jails protestors.
newsitem.headline: Albania to ban pyramid schemes, jails protestors.

text.p: Albania's right-wing government promised on Wednesday to ban pyramid investment schemes but a court jailed and fined demonstrators who mounted protests against them in central Tirana at the weekend.
Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu said during a trip to Lisbon that the government planned to push a law through parliament on Thursday to abolish the get-rich-quick schemes that led to street clashes.
"Tomorrow a special law will be approved in parliament," Shehu told a news conference. "We will take all the necessary measures to restore equilibrium."
Asked if the law would abolish the pyramid schemes, he said: "Yes."

He said the government had created a commission on Tuesday to study ways to pay compensation to those who had lost money. Authorities have already ordered the seizure of 25.5 billion leks ($255 million) deposited by such schemes in state-owned banks.
Thousands fearing that they could face the total loss of their life savings through collapsing schemes struggled with baton-wielding police during a protest in Tirana on Sunday.
Some demonstrators were hurt in the clashes and some 52 others were jailed or given hefty fines on charges of joining what judicial authorities said was an illegal protest.

Tirana district court's chief judge Qazim Gjonaj said 13 out of 54 defendants had been sentenced to between one and two weeks in jail for participating in an illegal demonstration. The others were fined 5,000 to 20,000 leks (about $50-200). Two were acquitted.

"After five trials, sentences were handed out to those detained last Sunday after an illegal gathering in defiance of a warning. Such actions are punishable with up to three months imprisonment according to the penal code," Gjonaj told Reuters.
The fines could wipe out more than a month's wages for some defendants with the average Albanian monthly salary at around 8,000 leks ($73).
Shehu said popular anger with the pyramid schemes did not threaten the government of President Sali Berisha.
"The pyramid schemes are not capable of destabilising the political, economic and financial system in Albania as the development of the Albanian economy was never based on such schemes," he said.

The Socialist daily Zeri i Popullit said the state had started proceedings against opposition leaders who led the protest. In response, the party would attempt to sue the state for using violence during the demonstration, it added.

The Socialists have called for peaceful protests over the next two days in the western city of Durres and in Tirana "in continuing support for popular protests because of the deepening (pyramid) scheme crisis".
Pyramid schemes burgeoned in Albania after the fall of communism in 1990, luring thousands of Albanians into selling their homes, land and livestock with promises of big returns.
But three of them have crumbled so far, leaving thousands out of pocket. Four more have suspended payments to investors.
